newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges off lows but still weak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges off lows but still weak.

text.p: London's October white sugar contract recovered slightly during thin afternoon trading after a mixed bag of sellers pressured the spot price down towards initial support at around $323 per tonne.
But activity was generally subdued with just 492 lots on the board by 1442 GMT, with one European broker cited as dominant among the sellers.
Traders said October's bounce from $323.10 late on Tuesday after light fund selling had shown that the contract was well supported with more upside potential.

"I don't foresee it coming down with great speed," said one. Fund players are still thought to be long in October after the concerted buying seen in late July which drove the contract to a fresh life-high of $331.00.
October was down 90 cents at $324.30 after moving in a tight $1.50 range. December was thinly traded, down $1.20 at $320.90, and trade crosses dominated the March volume.
Traders said there was little interest in the October/March spread, whose two positions accounted for the bulk of the session volume.
The Paris market was very quiet with just 202 lots of October on the board. The contract was down 60 cents at $323.80.
